question: What was the Western Schism (1378-1417), and how was it resolved?

choices.A: A period when there were two or three simultaneous claimants to the papacy; resolved by the Council of Constance (1414-1418) which accepted the resignation or removal of rival claimants and elected Martin V
choices.B: The split between Rome and Constantinople in 1054
choices.C: The Protestant Reformation, which permanently divided Western Christianity
choices.D: A dispute over the Crusades that caused France to break from Rome for 40 years

teaching.title: The Western Schism (1378-1417)
teaching.body: The Western Schism (not to be confused with the 1054 East-West Schism) began when, after the death of Gregory XI (who ended the Avignon papacy), the cardinals elected Urban VI — then, dissatisfied, elected a second pope (Clement VII) who returned to Avignon. Eventually a third claimant was added at the Council of Pisa (1409). The Council of Constance (1414-1418) resolved the crisis through 'conciliarism' — asserting that a general council has authority over the pope. Martin V was elected as the single legitimate pope in 1417. The crisis raised difficult questions about papal authority and ecclesiology.
